kicad_symbol_check: all 14 pins match ds p10 (1 AGND, 2 BIAS, 3 T-, 4 T+, 5 AVDD, 6 DNC, 7 DRDY, 8 DVDD, 9 CS, 10 SCK, 11 SDO, 12 SDI, 13 FAULT, 14 DGND)

circuit.role: optional series resistors / ferrite in each lead for RF pick-up (keep them equal; bias current 5.5 nA max)
circuit.page: p11: 'additional filtering and/or protection components may be added'; p3

circuit.role: CS pull-up so the chip stays deselected while the expander is unconfigured

supplies.AVDD=DVDD: 3.0-3.6 V, within 100 mV of each other

logic: 3.3 V SPI, clock polarity either way (modes 1 and 3; p6)
placement: The cold junction is measured by the chip itself: put it within a few millimetres of the thermocouple contacts, on the same copper, away from heat and draughts, with no heat-producing part nearby (p12).

Connector: no miniature thermocouple socket was found in JLCPCB's library (searched 'PCC-SMP', 'thermocouple connector'). Use two plated pads/a 2-pin position on the bench header edge; a K-type mini plug adapter can be a pigtail. Copper pads add an error only if the two pads sit at different temperatures: keep them close together and symmetric.
notes: Inputs survive +-45 V (p1-2); open-circuit and over/under-voltage faults are detected on chip.

CONFLICT to settle: the pin plan gives the chip select to a port expander but names no SPI bus. Proposed: the radio SPI (LPSPI6, 3.3 V pads). The memory/SDR SPI is on 1.8 V pads and the e-paper SPI has no data-in pad. A select line on an I2C expander costs two I2C writes per transfer (fine at a few readings per second) and the radio drivers must not use the bus in between.
It must stay powered whenever that SPI bus is active (an unpowered chip would load MISO/MOSI): always-on 3.3 V, 5 uA standby.
unverified: Whether SDO is high-impedance with CS high (expected for a shared bus; not found on the pages read).
